categories.main_business_segments: Siward Technology Co., Ltd. primarily engages in the research, development, design, production, sales, and after-sales service of quartz crystal components and oscillators. Their products mainly serve computer information products and communication equipment, functioning as fundamental signal sources. The company also involves in manufacturing quartz raw materials and import-export trade related to these products.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company utilizes advanced quartz crystal manufacturing processes including synthetic quartz bar production, chip cleaning, electrode sputtering, frequency adjustment, and packaging with aging tests. They emphasize miniaturization, high frequency, and high precision in their quartz crystal and oscillator designs, including MEMS technology and tuning fork wafer production. Automated SMT assembly and strict quality control systems are integral to their production.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include manufacturers in the computer, communication, consumer electronics, automotive, and medical device sectors. Major end markets are smartphones (including 5G devices), automotive electronics (such as TPMS and ADAS systems), wireless communication infrastructure (5G base stations, WiFi 7), wearable devices, and smart medical equipment. The company targets OEM and ODM clients primarily in Europe, Asia, and the Americas.
categories.geographic_coverage: Siward operates mainly in Taiwan with manufacturing facilities in Taichung, Tainan (Southern Taiwan Science Park), and Miaoli. It has subsidiaries and sales offices in Japan, China (Shenzhen, Wuxi), and the United States. The company’s sales are distributed across Asia, Europe, the Americas, and Taiwan, with strategic focus on expanding in the US and European markets while reducing reliance on China.
categories.supply_chain_position: Siward operates primarily in the midstream segment of the supply chain, producing quartz crystals and oscillators from raw quartz materials. It vertically integrates upstream by manufacturing synthetic quartz bars and quartz wafers, ensuring control over raw material quality and supply. Downstream, it supplies components to OEMs in electronics and communication industries.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company prioritizes R&D in miniaturized, high-frequency, and high-precision quartz components, including development of small-sized automotive TPMS crystals, high-frequency oscillators for optical communications, and low-voltage compensated oscillators for wearable devices. It invests about 6% of revenue in R&D, focusing on 5G/WiFi7 applications, automotive electronics, medical devices, and satellite communications. Collaboration with international partners and technology transfer are key to innovation.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated primarily through product sales of quartz crystals, oscillators, and related components. The company also earns from manufacturing services and after-sales support. It does not rely on subscription or licensing models but focuses on volume sales to OEMs and strategic partners globally.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Siward competes with Japanese and Chinese quartz component manufacturers. Japanese firms lead in technology and scale but have higher costs, while Chinese competitors compete aggressively on price with lower technology levels. Siward’s competitive advantages include vertical integration, diversified product lines, and strong R&D capabilities, positioning it as a mid-sized player with about 10% market share in Taiwan’s listed quartz industry.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: The company reported consolidated revenues of approximately NT$2.19 billion in 2024, reflecting a 7% decline from the previous year due to market softness and price competition. Net profit declined by about 39%. It maintains strong liquidity with a current ratio near 389%. R&D spending is around NT$121 million annually. The company plans to increase R&D investment to NT$140 million in 2025 to support growth in high-end markets.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Siward emphasizes vertical integration to control raw material quality and supply, enabling stable production and delivery. Its product differentiation lies in miniaturization, high precision, and high stability of quartz components, supported by advanced MEMS technology and tuning fork designs. The company targets high-growth sectors like 5G, automotive electronics, and medical devices, offering customized solutions with strong quality assurance and compliance with international environmental and automotive standards.
